Fracking KZN

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
KZN residents are angry about a recent plan to give exploration rights for oil and gas across vast areas of KZN

Summary:
A one-man show run from a shared office block in Cape Town has obtained the largest exploration rights in KwaZulu-Natal. 
Rhino Oil and Gas Exploration South Africa, which has its corporate office in the known tax haven of the British Virgin Islands, and with no known black economic empowerment partner, has landed not only a 1,5-million hectare exploration right in KZN, but similar rights in the Free State and Eastern Cape covering 73 876 km². The company also boasts off-shore rights in Namibia, the Western Cape and Senegal.
With the multinational subsidiary’s notice of application for environmental authorisation lambasted in the media recently, environmentalists have hit back, citing the vagueness surrounding the exploration as a major cause of concern. Rhino Oil and Gas Exploration South African director Phillip Steyn operates from a single office in Cape Town’s Icon Building, with no secretary and works off a Gmail account.

The company had recently lodged an application for an exploration right with Petroleum Agency South Africa (Pasa).
Oil, gas, condensate, coal bed methane, helium and biogenic gas are some of the minerals the exploration hopes to uncover through seismic surveys and drilling planned for three years.
The company has maintained that fracking is not envisaged.
The exploration in KZN will include approximately 10 000 farms in areas like Richmond, Ladysmith, Dundee, Mooi River, Estcourt, New Hanover, Ashburton, Ulundi and Nkandla.


Further information:
Environmentalists have slammed the move over concerns of potential fracking that may lead to widescale damage to the ecosystem. KZN-based NPO groundWork’s Bobby Peek said Rhino Oil and Gas Exploration have been “minimalistic” on what they intend to do if valuable minerals are found in KZN. “They [Rhino] might say there is no possibility of fracking, but what they are looking for could be fracked in the future,” Peek said.

Peek added even though farmers have a say in terms of negotiating drilling on their farms, farmers who have not applied for the rights to mine on their farms or have not used their right, could be overpowered by anyone who obtains the permission to do so.
Acting chair of the Midlands Conservancy Forum Sarah Allan said they are concerned about the affect of the exploration on key water resources in KZN.
“The drilling has potential for a huge impact on the quality and quantity of underground water resources which will in turn have a catastrophic impact on local agriculture,” Allan said.
A REPORT released by SLR Consulting, the independant environmental assessment practitioner for the project, shows the following preliminary issues and potential impacts have been identified and will be investigated as part of the environmental assessment process.
Concerns raised are as follows:

Farm safety – access by unknown persons to farms has the potential to cause security risks on farms. Operating heavy vehicles and equipment may pose safety risks. Runaway fires may present a potential safety risks for both people and livestock.
• Farm infrastructure – farms roads, gates and fences may be damaged during exploration activity.
• Soil and land capability– activities at the seismic and drill sites may affect soils and land capability if poorly regulated and not rehabilitated.
• Biodiversity — activities at the seismic and drill sites have the potential to disturb and or destroy vegetation, habitat units and related ecosystem functionality, including the disturbance of protected species.
• Surface water — the proposed activities at the seismic and drill sites has the potential to pollute surface water resources through consumptive use and the discharge of contaminants.
• Groundwater — the proposed drilling has the potential to consume and contaminate groundwater resources, which could impact availability to other groundwater users and the ecosystem.
• Air — the proposed project has the potential to contribute to air pollution, particularly through dust emissions from vehicles on gravel roads and the release of gas from boreholes.
• Noise and vibrations — the proposed project has the potential to cause noise pollution during drilling activities. Seismic surveys may cause damage to structures and disturb livestock and wildlife.
• Socio-economic — the project has very limited potential to contribute towards socio-economic impacts, mainly because local people do not have the scarce skills required and migrant labour will have to be imported.
While positive impacts include job creation and stimulation of the local and regional economy, the potential negative socio-economic impacts include potential for increased crime, spread of disease and pressure on support services provision.
The Umzimvubu Catchment Partnership (UCP), an alliance of 34 local communities with straddles KZN and the Eastern Cape says it believes if Rhino Oil and Gas Exploration South Africa is granted permission to proceed with the early-phase exploration, it will lead to hydrological fracturing.
“We need farming, not fracking,” said UCP secretary Nicky McLeod, who is also an environmental scientist.
The mountains where the exploration is set to take place form part of the Drakensberg range bordering Lesotho. According to the map that is part of Rhino’s application, the area to be explored goes right up to the Ongeluksnek Wetlands which McLeod says replenish underground water for boreholes that supply water to local communities and also feed into the uMzimvubu River, providing water to many people downstream.
“The uMzimvubu system has been earmarked for a major water storage initiative and potentially even hydroelectric capacity. Unfortunately fracking and water conservation do not work together The fracking process needs up to 20 million litres of water per fracking well,” she said.
McLeod says studies done in countries where fracking has taken place show the negatives far out- weigh the benefits.
Tello Lephuthing is one of the people who support the idea of mining as he says it will provide employment and other benefits to the mostly rural communities

Press Release:


Fracking KZN
KZN residents are fuming. Recent public participation meetings reached boiling point when land owners, community leaders, students and environmentalists vehemently opposed a bid to explore 1.5-million hectares of land for oil and gas. Applicants Rhino Oil and Gas say that there is tremendous excitement about these untapped oil and gas resources and unlocking those for our benefit may well become a reality. Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


FRACKING FINAL SCRIPT FOR TX FRIDAY 12 FEB

Commentary one
You may know the KZN midlands as a peaceful place of rolling hills, gentle farmlands and spectacular scenery

Up sound
F.. R.. A.. C.. K – don’t frack ….you never go back

But last November it was punctuated with pockets of fury ( lions river)

Nov meeting
Excuse me! You are totally unprepared! …people standing outside… can hear the nonsense you want to share with us

Commentary Two
Their anger was directed at a company called Rhino oil and gas, who announced their intention to explore for oil, gas, coal bed methane, helium and biogenic gas, and THAT in the minds of locals, meant fracking

Andisile Mqulo Student UKZN
I was hoping to get more information about the company, but it was not productive is another reason for concern

LINK
Not much is known about Rhino oil and gas except that it is a Texas company, founded by an American lawyer and its headed up in SA by a free state born man Phillip Steyn.

Commentary three
Phillip Steyn has been sent an open letter asking how he sleeps at night

Phillip
We are moving forward because we believe that by creating a domestic oil and gas industry it will be 100% to the benefit of everyone in South Africa, and I can sleep
very well at night ma’am!

Commentary four
Phillip Steyn and Texas attorney Patrick J. Mulligan are the only directors of Rhino oil and gas. Their company is a subsidiary of Rhino resources whose corporate headquarters are in the British Virgin Islands.

Phillip
Our financials are privately owned company we do not have to divulge that to anyone

up sound Lions River meeting
“You’ve got your response! The community has come out in numbers. Whose against fracking?

Cheering up sound

LINK
To frack or not to frack? That is the question, but there are mixed messages coming from Rhino. All they will commit to is that they are at the start of a three- year exploration to determine if there is gas and oil lurking beneath the green hills of KZN

Commentary five
Rhino insist they wont be fracking- for now. What they want to do is sink a maximum of ten core holes over the next three years and make use of a variety of techniques such as seismic testing they say are non invasive. Environmental lawyer Jeremy Ridl is skeptical

Jeremy RIdl
My concern and why I want to stop the process now, is that quite frankly I don’t trust government.

Commentary six
Jeremy wants to interdict the EIA process from continuing, because he says its irrational to allow exploration rights in areas where government’s own regulations protects water resources from fracking

Jeremy
If the EIA proceeds they are going to get the exploration rights, if they get the exploration rights they will find gas – if they find gas irrespective of these restrictions that have been imposed they will be allowed to extract and our worst fears will be realized

Commentary seven
Rhino are keeping their options open and wont say exactly which gas they are targeting, but geologists we spoke to say the most likely gas they will find is coal bed methane. In Australia extracting this gas has become a major industry. This documentary: Fractured country, explains the process

Up Sound docci
Explanation of how coal bed methane fracking works

Commentary eight
Rhino tell us that that these gas finds could save our economy, but in Queensland Australia farmers watched helplessly as their land changed forever

Up sound Fractured land
Living in a gas field this is hell ….honestly we don’t know what is going to happen

Commentary nine
This week our mining minister Mosebenze Zwane said that South Africa has relatively good prospects for upstream oil and gas development including shale gas.



Francois
If we allow this process to continue I think it will be the single biggest disaster to hit this country

Commentary ten
Francois Du Toit was one of the first locals to raise the alarm when Rhino oil and gas organized the public participation meetings

Francois
I think they had hoped that they would get away with small venues, no real resistance/ they got a helluva shock

Link
You may ask how a company ….heartland has a concession to dig deep into KZN heartlands and the area they want to mine is huge

Commentary eleven
Ten thousand farms, 1.5 million hectares- stretching from Richmond in the south to Ladysmith and Dundee in the north west. It extends almost to Ulundi and includes regions around Tugela Ferry and Nkandla

Up sound Bobby at November meeting
“outsourcing my democracy to consultants”

Commentary twelve
Bobby Peek, Groundwork’s director has been at several of the meetings

Derek to Bobby
You see this as making money on speculation?
Bobby
Unquestionably – 10 000 farms – so you find one or two farms you speculate and suddenly a small company makes a hell of a lot of profit because now Rhino oil and gas can sell off to shell and so there are a lot of small players all over SA hoping to strike it rich

Commentary thirteen
Rhino has five application’s across South Africa. They are just one of many companies applying for gas exploration from the Petroleum agency of SA.

Francois
Its like a gold rush but now it’s a gas rush or a mineral rush or petroleum rush what we are talking about in KZN is cutting across 3 of our major water sources if you look at bid docs its cutting across the Umzimvubu, the Umgeni and the Tugela

Commentary Fourteen
Already KZN is critically short of water and the Umgeni cannot provide enough. Yet Fracking will need millions more litres of water, and there are fears of contamination



Francois
I have no clue how any company is going to extract any kind of gas without infringing on the existing rights of water users

Commentary fifteen
This is the area under exploration, but if the government abides by its own rules then these little black spots represent the only areas they could legally frack should they discover gas

Jeremy
It is those areas only that the exploration company would be entitled to sink their exploration wells
Derek
In other words, don’t prospect where you can’t mine?
Jeremy
Absolutely so! in order to get your rights for your exploration right you involve people that cannot be affected at the end of the day

LINK
Rhino say they take all environmental issues very seriously. In order to gain the public’s trust they have employed an independent environmental company- SLR. Already SLR have noted a range of possible negative impacts on this document- but they wont speak to us and we don’t really understand why

Commentary sixteen
Phillip Steyn also refused media requests, but we had questions, so off we went to this meeting in Howick on the 2nd of February.

Up sound No fracking chanting outside Howick west Hall

Commentary seventeen
This time Rhino were more organized and Phillip stood by with his presentation

Disruption as man interrupts and shouts

In the heat tempers flared

Matthew
If you don’t want the meeting that’s fine we can close the meeting. Can I finish speaking?! can I finish speaking?!

Commentary eighteen
residents wanted questions before they would even listen

Question first lady
What happens when you drilling, can you tell me exactly because I want to know!
Question young student
How are you going to avoid water contamination with this?
Question black guy
People have given you facts! people have walked rivers! people have lived here! you are from the free state! You represent TEXAS!

Question petition lady
…..Get the hell out of KZN

LINK Derek walks out
Well emotions are at a boiling point, and its not just the sweltering heat more than an hour of protests and interjections and we still haven’t got to the presentation by rhino oil and gas

Commentary eighteen
That day Phillip never did finish his presentation. Residents are still not satisfied that Rhino have not answered concerns listed in their own documents – like increased crime, polluted surface and ground water, air pollution, destruction of habitats and vegetation

Up sound Nikki
Damaged structures, I am sorry its what you said

Yay!!!

Commentary Nineteen
Rhino are hoping for a favourable answer from the Petroleum agency of South Africa by mid June. But nervous residents are hoping the beautiful green hills of the midlands will never end up looking like these areas in Queensland Australia

10 mins 08 seconds

In at 00 01 00 00
Out at 00 11 08 00
Duration 10 08

Promo one in at 00 11 30 00
Promo two in at 12 00 00
Promo three in at 13 00 00

PROMO ONE 10 seconds
Fury in KZN over an application for oil, gas and Coal bed methane

Meeting up sound

PROMO TWO
Residents of KZN are demanding answers of a gas prospecting company

Black guy
People have given you facts people have lived here people have walked rivers
You’re from the free state – you represent TEXAS!




PROMO THREE
Will fracking become the new gold rush

Francois
Its like a gold rush but now it’s a gas rush or a mineral rush or petroleum rush
Bobby
so there are a lot of small players all over SA hoping to strike it rich

Phillip Our financials are privately owned company we do not have to divulge that to anyone up sound Lions River meeting “You’ve got your response! The community has come out in numbers. Whose against fracking? Cheering up sound LINK To frack or not to frack? That is the question, but there are mixed messages coming from Rhino. All they will commit to is that they are at the start of a three- year exploration to determine if there is gas and oil lurking beneath the green hills of KZN Commentary five Rhino insist they wont be fracking- for now. What they want to do is sink a maximum of ten core holes over the next three years and make use of a variety of techniques such as seismic testing they say are non invasive. Environmental lawyer Jeremy Ridl is skeptical Jeremy RIdl My concern and why I want to stop the process now, is that quite frankly I don’t trust government. Commentary six Jeremy wants to interdict the EIA process from continuing, because he says its irrational to allow exploration rights in areas where government’s own regulations protects water resources from fracking Jeremy If the EIA proceeds they are going to get the exploration rights, if they get the exploration rights they will find gas – if they find gas irrespective of these restrictions that have been imposed they will be allowed to extract and our worst fears will be realized Commentary seven Rhino are keeping their options open and wont say exactly which gas they are targeting, but geologists we spoke to say the most likely gas they will find is coal bed methane. In Australia extracting this gas has become a major industry. This documentary: Fractured country, explains the process Up Sound docci Explanation of how coal bed methane fracking works Commentary eight Rhino tell us that that these gas finds could save our economy, but in Queensland Australia farmers watched helplessly as their land changed forever Up sound Fractured land Living in a gas field this is hell ….honestly we don’t know what is going to happen Commentary nine This week our mining minister Mosebenze Zwane said that South Africa has relatively good prospects for upstream oil and gas development including shale gas. Francois If we allow this process to continue I think it will be the single biggest disaster to hit this country Commentary ten Francois Du Toit was one of the first locals to raise the alarm when Rhino oil and gas organized the public participation meetings Francois I think they had hoped that they would get away with small venues, no real resistance/ they got a helluva shock Link You may ask how a company ….heartland has a concession to dig deep into KZN heartlands and the area they want to mine is huge Commentary eleven Ten thousand farms, 1.5 million hectares- stretching from Richmond in the south to Ladysmith and Dundee in the north west. It extends almost to Ulundi and includes regions around Tugela Ferry and Nkandla Up sound Bobby at November meeting “outsourcing my democracy to consultants” Commentary twelve Bobby Peek, Groundwork’s director has been at several of the meetings Derek to Bobby You see this as making money on speculation? Bobby Unquestionably – 10 000 farms – so you find one or two farms you speculate and suddenly a small company makes a hell of a lot of profit because now Rhino oil and gas can sell off to shell and so there are a lot of small players all over SA hoping to strike it rich Commentary thirteen Rhino has five application’s across South Africa. They are just one of many companies applying for gas exploration from the Petroleum agency of SA. Francois Its like a gold rush but now it’s a gas rush or a mineral rush or petroleum rush what we are talking about in KZN is cutting across 3 of our major water sources if you look at bid docs its cutting across the Umzimvubu, the Umgeni and the Tugela Commentary Fourteen Already KZN is critically short of water and the Umgeni cannot provide enough. Yet Fracking will need millions more litres of water, and there are fears of contamination Francois I have no clue how any company is going to extract any kind of gas without infringing on the existing rights of water users Commentary fifteen This is the area under exploration, but if the government abides by its own rules then these little black spots represent the only areas they could legally frack should they discover gas Jeremy It is those areas only that the exploration company would be entitled to sink their exploration wells Derek In other words, don’t prospect where you can’t mine? Jeremy Absolutely so! in order to get your rights for your exploration right you involve people that cannot be affected at the end of the day LINK Rhino say they take all environmental issues very seriously. In order to gain the public’s trust they have employed an independent environmental company- SLR. Already SLR have noted a range of possible negative impacts on this document- but they wont speak to us and we don’t really understand why Commentary sixteen Phillip Steyn also refused media requests, but we had questions, so off we went to this meeting in Howick on the 2nd of February. Up sound No fracking chanting outside Howick west Hall Commentary seventeen This time Rhino were more organized and Phillip stood by with his presentation Disruption as man interrupts and shouts In the heat tempers flared Matthew If you don’t want the meeting that’s fine we can close the meeting. Can I finish speaking?! can I finish speaking?! Commentary eighteen residents wanted questions before they would even listen Question first lady What happens when you drilling, can you tell me exactly because I want to know! Question young student How are you going to avoid water contamination with this? Question black guy People have given you facts! people have walked rivers! people have lived here! you are from the free state! You represent TEXAS! Question petition lady …..Get the hell out of KZN LINK Derek walks out Well emotions are at a boiling point, and its not just the sweltering heat more than an hour of protests and interjections and we still haven’t got to the presentation by rhino oil and gas Commentary eighteen That day Phillip never did finish his presentation. Residents are still not satisfied that Rhino have not answered concerns listed in their own documents – like increased crime, polluted surface and ground water, air pollution, destruction of habitats and vegetation Up sound Nikki Damaged structures, I am sorry its what you said Yay!!! metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): KZN residents are angry about a recent plan to give exploration rights for oil and gas across vast areas of KZN
metadata.Summary: A one-man show run from a shared office block in Cape Town has obtained the largest exploration rights in KwaZulu-Natal. Rhino Oil and Gas Exploration South Africa, which has its corporate office in the known tax haven of the British Virgin Islands, and with no known black economic empowerment partner, has landed not only a 1,5-million hectare exploration right in KZN, but similar rights in the Free State and Eastern Cape covering 73 876 km². The company also boasts off-shore rights in Namibia, the Western Cape and Senegal. With the multinational subsidiary’s notice of application for environmental authorisation lambasted in the media recently, environmentalists have hit back, citing the vagueness surrounding the exploration as a major cause of concern. Rhino Oil and Gas Exploration South African director Phillip Steyn operates from a single office in Cape Town’s Icon Building, with no secretary and works off a Gmail account. The company had recently lodged an application for an exploration right with Petroleum Agency South Africa (Pasa). Oil, gas, condensate, coal bed methane, helium and biogenic gas are some of the minerals the exploration hopes to uncover through seismic surveys and drilling planned for three years. The company has maintained that fracking is not envisaged. The exploration in KZN will include approximately 10 000 farms in areas like Richmond, Ladysmith, Dundee, Mooi River, Estcourt, New Hanover, Ashburton, Ulundi and Nkandla.
metadata.Further information: Environmentalists have slammed the move over concerns of potential fracking that may lead to widescale damage to the ecosystem. KZN-based NPO groundWork’s Bobby Peek said Rhino Oil and Gas Exploration have been “minimalistic” on what they intend to do if valuable minerals are found in KZN. “They [Rhino] might say there is no possibility of fracking, but what they are looking for could be fracked in the future,” Peek said. Peek added even though farmers have a say in terms of negotiating drilling on their farms, farmers who have not applied for the rights to mine on their farms or have not used their right, could be overpowered by anyone who obtains the permission to do so. Acting chair of the Midlands Conservancy Forum Sarah Allan said they are concerned about the affect of the exploration on key water resources in KZN. “The drilling has potential for a huge impact on the quality and quantity of underground water resources which will in turn have a catastrophic impact on local agriculture,” Allan said. A REPORT released by SLR Consulting, the independant environmental assessment practitioner for the project, shows the following preliminary issues and potential impacts have been identified and will be investigated as part of the environmental assessment process. Concerns raised are as follows: Farm safety – access by unknown persons to farms has the potential to cause security risks on farms. Operating heavy vehicles and equipment may pose safety risks. Runaway fires may present a potential safety risks for both people and livestock. • Farm infrastructure – farms roads, gates and fences may be damaged during exploration activity. • Soil and land capability– activities at the seismic and drill sites may affect soils and land capability if poorly regulated and not rehabilitated. • Biodiversity — activities at the seismic and drill sites have the potential to disturb and or destroy vegetation, habitat units and related ecosystem functionality, including the disturbance of protected species. • Surface water — the proposed activities at the seismic and drill sites has the potential to pollute surface water resources through consumptive use and the discharge of contaminants. • Groundwater — the proposed drilling has the potential to consume and contaminate groundwater resources, which could impact availability to other groundwater users and the ecosystem. • Air — the proposed project has the potential to contribute to air pollution, particularly through dust emissions from vehicles on gravel roads and the release of gas from boreholes. • Noise and vibrations — the proposed project has the potential to cause noise pollution during drilling activities. Seismic surveys may cause damage to structures and disturb livestock and wildlife. • Socio-economic — the project has very limited potential to contribute towards socio-economic impacts, mainly because local people do not have the scarce skills required and migrant labour will have to be imported. While positive impacts include job creation and stimulation of the local and regional economy, the potential negative socio-economic impacts include potential for increased crime, spread of disease and pressure on support services provision. The Umzimvubu Catchment Partnership (UCP), an alliance of 34 local communities with straddles KZN and the Eastern Cape says it believes if Rhino Oil and Gas Exploration South Africa is granted permission to proceed with the early-phase exploration, it will lead to hydrological fracturing. “We need farming, not fracking,” said UCP secretary Nicky McLeod, who is also an environmental scientist. The mountains where the exploration is set to take place form part of the Drakensberg range bordering Lesotho. According to the map that is part of Rhino’s application, the area to be explored goes right up to the Ongeluksnek Wetlands which McLeod says replenish underground water for boreholes that supply water to local communities and also feed into the uMzimvubu River, providing water to many people downstream. “The uMzimvubu system has been earmarked for a major water storage initiative and potentially even hydroelectric capacity. Unfortunately fracking and water conservation do not work together The fracking process needs up to 20 million litres of water per fracking well,” she said. McLeod says studies done in countries where fracking has taken place show the negatives far out- weigh the benefits. Tello Lephuthing is one of the people who support the idea of mining as he says it will provide employment and other benefits to the mostly rural communities
